data.G: No integration yet. Keep the validated baseline as a fallback; compare only correctly validated candidates and independently confirm the final integrated program. Do not assume gains combine additively.
data.analysis: Choose N=3 for complementary opportunities: the source exposes both an expensive block-local reduction and a multi-stage large-input schedule, while small inputs have a distinct launch/copy cost. The baseline is valid and correct: mean 46.7866 μs across three samples, score 0.5. The current 128-thread kernel uses modulo-based shared-memory reduction with repeated block barriers; at n=4194304 it launches four reduction stages (32768→256→2→1) and then copies the result. These are optimization hypotheses, not proof of bottlenecks. Use only the supplied GH200/CUDA 12.6.3 target facts; preserve exact results for current input, all supported n, device-only execution, default stream, and uninitialized scratch. The CUDA 12.6.3 guide describes synchronization through explicit cooperating groups; do not rely on implicit cross-block ordering or stale scratch contents. Reference: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.6.3/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore replacing only the CTA-local reduction in reduce0 with a warp-centric or permitted CUB block reduction. Keep the existing launch geometry, one input per lane, and multi-stage scratch schedule to isolate the block-reduction change. Handle tail lanes safely and preserve exact signed integer sums. Validate all checks and compare complete-run timings, especially at the performance size.
children.subject: Reduce CTA synchronization while preserving the existing launch schedule

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore a large-n reduction schedule that reduces the number of kernel stages by tuning elements per CTA and partial-sum count. Ensure the first stage has enough parallel CTAs and the final stage writes the result directly to out where beneficial. Every scratch value read must have been written during that call; do not depend on uninitialized scratch or cross-CTA ordering. Preserve a correct path for all supported n and compare total-run timings.
children.subject: Reduce large-input kernel stages and final-copy overhead

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, explore a measured size-based path for small positive n that computes from the current input in one device kernel and writes directly to out, avoiding scratch and the separate result copy where profitable. Select a generic crossover from measurements, not exact test sizes, and retain a correct large-input path. Validate every check and compare complete-run timings.
children.subject: Add a direct small-input reduction path
